subsystems.name: Sensing element
subsystems.role: detects physical or chemical conditions in the environment.

subsystems.name: Microcontroller and radio
subsystems.role: processes sensor data and transmits it wirelessly.

subsystems.name: Power unit
subsystems.role: harvests energy from the surroundings and stores enough to operate intermittently.

subsystems.name: Packaging and deployment
subsystems.role: protects the mote and allows it to be dispersed over an area.

subsystems.name: Networking
subsystems.role: forms a mesh so motes can relay data to a base station.

buildSteps.title: Design and simulate
buildSteps.detail: Model the mote's size, power budget, sensing needs and communication range before fabrication.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate MEMS sensors
buildSteps.detail: Use semiconductor processes such as photolithography, etching and deposition to create microscopic mechanical structures on a silicon wafer.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the integrated circuit
buildSteps.detail: Build the microcontroller and radio using a CMOS process optimised for very low power.

buildSteps.title: Integrate energy harvesting
buildSteps.detail: Deposit or attach photovoltaic cells and piezoelectric cantilevers that convert light or vibration into electricity.

buildSteps.title: Add energy storage
buildSteps.detail: Form thin-film batteries or supercapacitors on-chip or as a stacked layer to buffer harvested energy.

buildSteps.title: Assemble and package
buildSteps.detail: Dice the wafer, stack sensor, circuit and power layers, wire-bond them, and encapsulate in a protective coating.

buildSteps.title: Test and calibrate
buildSteps.detail: Check each mote's sensitivity, power consumption and radio range in the lab, then calibrate the sensors.

buildSteps.title: Deploy and network
buildSteps.detail: Scatter motes over the target area, let them form a mesh network, and begin collecting and relaying data.

prerequisites.why: the same lithography and etching used for phone accelerometers can make millimetre-scale sensors.
protocols like Bluetooth Low Energy exist, but shrinking radios to millimetre scale while keeping range is still research.
solar cells and vibration harvesters work at small sizes, but typically produce only microwatts to milliwatts.
thin-film batteries and supercapacitors are improving, yet capacity per volume remains limited.
efficient antennas at millimetre scale are difficult because physics ties performance to wavelength.
routing data through thousands of tiny motes without collisions or excessive power draw is not yet routine.

pathway.milestone: laboratory prototypes of millimetre-scale computers that sense, compute and transmit
pathway.unlocks: proof that a complete mote can fit in a grain of sand.

pathway.milestone: field trials in precision agriculture and structural health monitoring
pathway.unlocks: real-world data on durability, range and maintenance.

pathway.milestone: commercial production with better energy harvesting and mesh networking
pathway.unlocks: cheap, disposable sensors for large-area monitoring.

pathway.milestone: biodegradable or self-powered motes that need no retrieval
pathway.unlocks: environmental and agricultural sensing at very large scale.
